threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You can spot the newcomers; they're the ones still baffled by the weekend Tube closures and trying to navigate the bus routes on their phones.
Caught the N155 last night—two blokes arguing over who saw a ghost in the back. Got off with a voucher for a kebab after they made up.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a group of kids playing with a disco ball in a park at noon, I knew I had found my home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Kreuzberg's spontaneous Kebab festivals showcase not just food, but a wild mix of art, music, and community that you won't find anywhere else.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only a true local knows that 'the cloud' isn't just about tech, but also about the fog rolling in and out of Dolores Park.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a full tuxedo at Larkin and Eddy, ready for a gala, but still waiting on a broken bus. Classic San Francisco—style meets struggle.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think 'pancakes' at brunch means sweet, but locals dip theirs in omelette. Different food culture, but they never notice.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They still look puzzled by the Mercat de Gràcia's layout, trying to figure out which stall has the best jamón.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the 'bus stop' signs are actual recommendations, not just polite suggestions.
Last night on the 345, two lads argued over who'd seen the best street art in Brixton. Turns out none of it was even real. Classic.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I spotted a guy in a full tuxedo riding a bike with a parrot on his shoulder past the tempelhof street market. Classic Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a hidden courtyard with a vintage record shop, an open-air library, and a taco truck all in one spot.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a local when they roll their eyes at tourists frantically snapping photos of the murals, but don’t even blink at the homeless guy who’s become part of the scenery.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a bus today that took a detour down a blocked street—drivers got mad, but the riders got a view of hidden murals. Classic San Francisco surprise.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Most tourists think Gràcia is just about Gaudí and hip bars; they miss how many locals simply sit on the steps of Plaça de la Vila, sharing stories and laughter.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by the way they stand in the middle of the street, completely baffled by how the taxi drivers navigate with zero patience.
